The goal: menu decisions that are faster, aligned and backed by data, from recipe pool to sign-off

Optimo redesign, leadership update, Nov 13, 2026

2 of 8

Core objective: A unified menu operations management tool to handle recipe planning, performance optimization, cost monitoring, and analytical review for meal kit brands in Canada.

FOR THE BUSINESS

One source of truth for menu work

Menu-related workflows consolidated into a single source of truth platform to be used by all stakeholders.

FOR CUSTOMERS

The best possible menu for each customer segment

Draft menus analyzed, optimized, and reviewed to ensure the best possible offering for each segment of customers.

FOR OUR TEAMS

One app and one cost, instead of side sheets

Culinary, Menu Planning and leadership plan, check and sign off in one app, on the same cost as budget and finance.

Faster: Pages load faster, and the work moves out of side sheets.

Aligned: One set of rules and one cost, the same as budget and finance.

Backed by data: Pool health, projected performance and swap cost in front of planners when they decide.

SAY: The goal is menu decisions that are faster, aligned and backed by data, from the recipe pool to sign-off. Today a lot of menu decisions rest on experience, because the data isn't in front of people when they decide; the goal is to put it there, in one place where Culinary, Menu Planning and leadership work on the same cost. For the business, that's one source of truth for menu work; for customers, every draft menu analysed and reviewed before it goes out; and for our teams, planning, checks and sign-off in one app, on the same cost as budget and finance.

SOURCES
- Core objective, business outcome, customer outcome: Niyanth's project template ([DRAFT] Optimo Executive Presentation, Sep 2026): core objective p4, business key outcome p6, customer key outcome p8. Kept word for word. The bold headlines are short plain-word versions of those lines ("single source of truth platform" → "One source of truth for menu work"; "the best possible offering for each segment of customers" → "The best possible menu for each customer segment").
- "Instead of side sheets": teams worked around Optimo in Google Sheets (requirements §2; slide 3).
- Goal wording (faster, aligned, backed by data): Afagh, Nov 9 ("more efficient, more aligned, less time consuming, and more data driven"). Framed as a goal: time saved is not measured.
- Faster: Menu Architecture 3–12 s instead of 46–64 s (CHANGELOG.md Nov 5); Menu Analytics about 50 s less on the first load of the day (Oct 21); Recipe Pool loads faster (Oct 28); side sheets: requirements §2. Aligned: rules from the master plan (CHANGELOG Nov 5); cost on Excelsior's logic (CHANGELOG Nov 3; Afagh Nov 9). Backed by data: Pool Dashboard (Oct 28), Menu Analytics projected performance, swap cost impact (plan c4; redesign draft).
- For our teams: who uses Optimo (Oct 30 director update, slide 2; requirements §2); same cost as budget and finance (Afagh, Nov 9: Excelsior's COGS is aligned with budget and finance, and every cost in Optimo will follow it).
- Goal framing: plan-data.json meta.vision and meta.goal.
- IF ASKED, what is it worth and how will we know it worked (moved from the old "Likely questions" slide): dollars, hours saved and adoption aren't measured yet, so the deck doesn't claim them. What's measured is speed and the cost method. Once swap cost is live, each swap shows how it changes the menu cost, which gives us something to track. Success means pages live, teams using them, and directors signing off on the menu review workflow. Sources: Afagh, Nov 5 (nothing measured in dollars, hours or adoption); CHANGELOG.md Oct 21, Nov 3, Nov 5; plan c4; plan-data.json meta.metrics ("Redesigned pages live"; "User adoption"; "Stakeholder sign-off: Directors sign off on menu review workflow").

Optimo is built to scale: new rules, data and brands plug into the same app, ready for personalization and global segments

Optimo redesign, leadership update, Nov 13, 2026

8 of 8

How Optimo scales

2027 candidates

Rules update from one master plan

Slot rules load daily from the product team’s master plan, so when the menu’s structure changes, Optimo follows without anyone re-entering rules.

New data plugs into existing pages

The pages read one shared recipe pool, so new data, like the global customer segments, can be added once and shown where it’s needed. The Pool Dashboard already has a place for a segment filter.

A new brand is a setting, not a new app

The brand is one setting in Menu Architecture and Recipe Validation, with Chef’s Plate kept apart. A brand that plans with GAMP would need its own master plan.

Analysis ready for personalization

Menu Analytics already shows composition, version comparison and projected performance for every menu: the weekly view planners expect to need once personalization reaches every customer.

Maybe, less likely

SAY: Optimo is built to scale after launch. Its rules load daily from the product team's master plan, its pages share one recipe pool so new data like the global segments can be added once, and a new brand is a setting plus its own master plan, not a new app. Menu Analytics already gives the weekly view of projected performance that planners expect to need once personalization reaches every customer, and the 2027 candidates on the right are to be discussed, scoped and planned in 2027.

SOURCES
- Rules update from one master plan: the master is the product team's Slot Breakdown sheet, loaded into a table every day (pages/menu_architecture/rules_store.py; CHANGELOG.md Nov 5). A week and GAMP version with no copy shows the master.
- New data plugs into existing pages: one shared recipe pool loader (data/data_fetcher.py get_recipe_pool_data) is used by Recipe Pool, Menu Architecture's slot plan, Recipe Validation, Menu Review, the swap tab and Final Menu. The Pool Dashboard's segment filter and segment × protein pivot are built but commented out "until a segment source exists" (pages/recipe_pool/pool_dashboard.py, Oct 28; plan s23, Irene Aug 27). "Can be added once and shown where it's needed" describes how the app is built, not a plan: segments have no finalized plan (Afagh, Nov 9).
- Global customer segmentation (context, not on the slide): a new segmentation model global is working on, based on customer taste profile; not the master plan's preference groups (Explorer, Harmonizer, Balanced, Collection 1/2) (Afagh, Nov 9).
- A new brand is a setting: pages/menu_architecture/page_config.py sets BRAND = "HelloFresh" in one place; rules_store.py keeps slots 4000 and up (Chef's Plate) apart. Chef's Plate doesn't plan its menus with GAMP (Afagh, Nov 9), so a brand would need its own master slot plan.
